Sprinklers at Culyer Gore Park in the Fort Greene neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City, at the corner of Fulton Street and Greene Avenue. The western part of the park was purchased by the city of Brooklyn in 1845 for $1, and was named for Dr. Theodore Ledyard Culyer, minister of the nearby PArk Presbyyterian Church and then the Lafayette Avenue Presbyterian Church. A statue of Dr. Culyer was planned, but he demurred. The park deteriorated in the 1960s and 70s, and was renovated in the 1980s. candidats.titre: File:Fire Sprinkler Alarm in Butler, PA.jpg
candidats.description: Fire sprinkler alarm, for fire sprinklers in a building in Butler, Pennsylvania . The alarm is designed to sound automatically if water in the sprinkler system starts to follow, which indicates either sprinkler head has been activated or a critical failure in the system, such as a broken pipe. These types of alarms are frequently simple in nature, consisting of a basic mechanical bell, and often will not contact the fire department.
